newsitem.title: MADAGASCAR: Madagascar suspends election result publication.
newsitem.headline: Madagascar suspends election result publication.

text.p: Madagascar's interior ministry has suspended publication of results in the run-off presidential election between former presidents Didier Ratsiraka and Albert Zafy after Zafy demanded a recount.

Boto Victor, the president of the Constitutional High Court which must ratify the election outcome, said on Monday evening on state television that the results published so far by the interior ministry were provisional.
Zafy, 69, had challenged the results that gave former military ruler Ratsiraka, 60, an unbeatable lead in the race for the presidency of the Indian Ocean island state of 14 million people.

According to the interior ministry Ratsiraka had 50.52 of the vote against Zafy's 49.48 percent, leaving the former military ruler 32,000 votes ahead. There are only some 30,000 votes left to be counted.
Ratification of the results lasts one month after January 13, the date for receipt of the final return from polling stations to the High Court.
"The High Court stands clearly on the totality of results coming from the voting stations themselves," said Boto.
Zafy told a news conference on Monday he demanded a recount of results from the December 29 second round election, saying some interior ministry officials were allied with Ratsiraka's party.
He said he had proof that the vote counting was rigged but did not want all results cancelled, only those issued by the National Electoral Committee since December 31.

Zafy's supporters last week accused officials of manipulating results in favour of Ratsiraka, a retired admiral and a former Marxist who ruled Madagascar for 16 years before losing to Zafy in the last presidential election in 1993.
Election observers from the Organisation of African Unity, the International Committee of Jurists and the Francophone Agency for Technical and Cultural Cooperation have said the election was normal.
The two-round presidential election was ordered after the parliament impeached Zafy for violating the constitution and exceeding his powers.
Zafy won the 1993 election after political unrest and subsequent repression paralysed the country for months.
Ratsiraka returned from 19 months in voluntary exile in France to contest the election after Zafy's impeachment.
Ratsiraka campaigned on promises of establishing a "humanistic and ecological republic" in Madagascar where most of the people live in chronic poverty.
